lines: Good morning. I’m Hannah Thibedeau, and this is your Palindrome News brief.
Premier Doug Ford may no longer be enjoying the Trump bump that propelled his popularity for months, a new poll suggests, Toronto Star reports.

Three leaders who view their nations as the world’s superpowers sat around a table together for the first time on Thursday to talk about reducing nuclear risks and resolving conflicts — a step they applauded as historic though, The Associated Press reports.
In a landmark judgment, the United Nations top court ruled Thursday that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority in a brutal 2017 military operation, The Associated Press reports.
Grand Theft Auto VI release means Surrey, B.C., landscaping company employees get the day off, The Canadian Press reports.
That’s your brief. We’ll keep watching, so you don’t have to.
